title: The scale
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: The derby's scale, borrowed from the cannery every year: a hanging brass thing with a hook. Gully hangs it from the shack's eave. It swings. He weighs the dog. Eleven pounds. The dog is entered.

panels.composition: The shack's eave. GULLY hanging a brass hanging scale with a hook from a nail. The half-lit string of lights still up. WOOD. BARNABY.

image.prompt: a stocky teenager hanging a brass hanging scale from a nail under a shack's eave beside a string of lights, a young man and a dog below, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The scale swinging. The needle at zero, then not.

image.prompt: close on a brass hanging scale swinging with its needle settling, black and white, no words

panels.composition: Gully lifting the dog by a loop of rope under the belly onto the hook. The dog's face: this is fine.

image.prompt: a teenager weighing a small dog in a rope sling on a hanging scale, the dog resigned, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The needle: 11. Gully writing it on the entrants' board. Under a column of names as blocks: BARNABY.

image.prompt: close on a chalk board of entrants' names rendered as blocks with one name legible at the bottom, black and white, no words
image.notes: Letter after: BARNABY — 11 (the only legible entry).

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: The dog is entered at eleven pounds. He doesn't win; he isn't a crab.
